title: Select base appearance needs improvements
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I played around with this some more and noticed a couple of things:

1. It's not immediately clear that when we say "The following styles are [expected](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#expected) to apply to [select](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered as a [drop-down box](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#drop-down-box) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance):" that applies to the `select` element and its subtree.
2. I'm also not sure how the above works with `::picker`. If `::picker` does not have `appearance: base`, the `option` elements are still part of the `select` element's subtree. So what then? (3 might also make this more complicated.)
3. <s>I don't think we can change the shadow tree of `select` elements depending on whether they are a dropdown or list box. That would make the shadow tree a function of base appearance. We probably have to generally define the shadow tree of `select` elements, regardless of base appearance. (This is really only observable with the inheritance games I think, but we might as well get it right and not have the specification say things we don't expect people to implement.)</s> This was wrong. Changing the shadow tree is possible as long as we (mostly?) don't use the shadow tree for native appearance purposes.
